answer: Each registrant must present a sealed enclave attestation whose serial number has never appeared in the registry, and the network admits only one identity per serial. An attacker must therefore forge or buy a distinct chip for every fake, roughly 400 units apiece with a three-week wait in the foundry queue. Chips from the same wafer lot are cross-checked, so a prism of identical devices lights up the audit, and one shared ember of suspicion can void the whole batch.
